problem: Symbolic regression suffers from exponential search space growth, with redundant exploration of syntactically different expressions that define the same function, slowing training.
approach: Introduces EGG-SR, which embeds symbolic equivalence into regression methods (MCTS, DRL, LLM) using equality graphs to compactly represent equivalent expressions, pruning redundancy and accelerating learning.
contribution: Demonstrates that EGG-SR consistently enhances symbolic regression across benchmarks, discovering more accurate expressions within the same time limit while tightening regret bounds for MCTS and reducing DRL gradient variance.

problem: LLMs used for tabular feature engineering act as black-box optimizers that lack calibrated utility estimates, leading to repeated exploration of low-yield operations without principled prioritization.
approach: Proposes a human-LLM collaborative framework that decouples proposal (LLM-generated candidates) from selection (guided by explicit utility modeling) and incorporates human preference feedback to identify more promising operations.
contribution: Improves feature engineering performance across tabular datasets and reduces user cognitive load, validated on both synthetic and real user studies.

problem: Multimodal editing large models fail to preserve facial identity consistency during portrait editing due to cross-source distribution bias and feature contamination, hindering practical deployment.
approach: Introduces EditedID, an alignment-disentanglement-entanglement framework using adaptive mixing for latent alignment, hybrid solvers for identity attribute disentanglement, and attentional gating for selective element entanglement.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance in preserving facial ID and edited element consistency as a training-free, plug-and-play solution for single/multi-person editing in open-world settings.

problem: Hierarchical federated learning topology selection remains open, as optimal configurations depend on complex interactions between data heterogeneity, network conditions, and client participation patterns.
approach: Establishes a unified convergence framework analyzing all four HFL topologies (Star-Star, Star-Ring, Ring-Star, Ring-Ring) under non-convex objectives with varying intra/inter-group data heterogeneity and full/partial client participation.
contribution: Reveals three fundamental topology selection principles: top-tier aggregation dominance, dependency on client grouping, and inter-group heterogeneity primacy, validated on CIFAR-10/CINIC-10/Fashion-MNIST/SST-2.

problem: LLM-based embeddings use encoder-only approaches that overlook generative strengths and miss latent concepts implicit in semantic representations.
approach: Introduces GIRCSE, which leverages autoregressive generation with iterative contrastive refinement to produce soft-token sequences optimized under contrastive objectives, capturing implicit semantics.
contribution: Outperforms strong LLM-based embedding baselines on MTEB benchmarks and exhibits emergent test-time scaling where generating more tokens steadily improves embedding quality.

problem: Frozen multimodal LLMs for video anomaly detection inherit pre-training biases and cannot adapt internal representations to specific contexts, limiting ability to handle subtle anomalies.
approach: Proposes SteerVAD, which identifies latent anomaly experts via gradient-free representational separability analysis and uses a hierarchical meta-controller to generate dynamic rectification signals that amplify anomaly-relevant dimensions.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance among tuning-free approaches while requiring only 1% of training data, establishing active representation steering as a new direction for VAD.

problem: Multimodal ecological learning from heterogeneous data sources (satellite, time series, tabular, bioacoustics) suffers from incomplete data and modality imbalance, where dominant modalities hinder optimization of others.
approach: Introduces MIAM, a dynamic masking strategy that explores full input combinations, prioritizes informative/challenging subsets, and adaptively increases masking of dominant modalities based on relative performance and learning dynamics.
contribution: Significantly improves robustness and predictive performance on GeoPlant and TaxaBench while enabling fine-grained contribution analysis revealing which variables and regions most strongly drive performance.

problem: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards fails in long-context scenarios because sparse outcome-only rewards provide insufficient gradient signal for the model to learn contextual grounding from external information.
approach: Proposes LongRLVR, augmenting sparse answer rewards with dense, verifiable context rewards that directly incentivize correct information selection, providing robust learning gradients for long-context reasoning.
contribution: Consistently outperforms standard RLVR across models (Qwen, LLaMA), boosting 14B model RULER-QA scores from 73.17 to 88.90 and LongBench v2 from 39.8 to 46.5.

problem: Quantum machine learning advantages have been proven for evaluation hardness but remain poorly understood for the learning process itself, especially for quantum functions without random-generation capability.
approach: Proves identification learning advantages for quantum functions under complexity-theoretic assumptions by developing a new proof strategy showing exponential advantage for broad quantum identification tasks.
contribution: Establishes first proofs of quantum identification learning advantages and conjecturally shows quantum functions are not random-generatable under plausible complexity assumptions.

problem: Masked diffusion models for language generation rely on ad hoc rule-based unmasking schedules (max-confidence, max-margin) that do not effectively adapt to data distributions or task requirements.
approach: Replaces heuristic schedules with a learned scheduler formulated as a KL-regularized MDP with explicit reference policy, optimizing a regularized objective with policy-improvement and convergence guarantees.
contribution: Proves learned policy generates samples closer to data distribution than heuristics, achieving 22% gain over random and 12% gain over max-confidence on SUDOKU with critical unmasking order.

problem: Training LLM agents via reinforcement learning faces sparse, unverifiable rewards and high-variance credit assignment when using explicit step labels or additional rollouts.
approach: Introduces iStar, which optimizes an implicit process reward model alongside policy using multi-turn DPO objective to generate implicit step rewards for each action, combining step-level with trajectory-level advantages.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art results on WebShop, VisualSokoban, and SOTOPIA benchmarks, demonstrating superior performance over frontier LLMs with higher sample efficiency.

problem: Learning dynamic causal structures is challenging because both instantaneous and lagged causal dependencies change over time, violating stationarity assumptions and destabilizing discovery methods.
approach: Introduces DyCausal, leveraging convolutional networks to model causal structures within coarse-grained time windows and linear interpolation to refine to each time step, with matrix-norm-based acyclic constraints.
contribution: Significantly outperforms existing methods on synthetic and real-world datasets, effectively identifying fully dynamic causal structures from coarse to fine temporal scales.

problem: Text-to-image diffusion models inherit cultural biases from training data and fail to faithfully depict underrepresented regions, with existing benchmarks focusing on object-centric categories rather than cultural activities.
approach: Introduces CULTIVate, a benchmark of 576 cross-cultural activity prompts spanning 16 countries with descriptor-based evaluation across cultural dimensions (background, attire, objects, interactions).
contribution: Proposes four metrics measuring cultural alignment, hallucination, exaggerated elements, and diversity, revealing systematic disparities favoring global north and enabling cultural faithfulness measurement.

problem: Ensuring factuality of LLM outputs is essential for safety in high-stakes domains, but existing conformal inference approaches are either overly conservative or rely on simple models that fail to capture complex group structures.
approach: Reformulates conformal inference in multiplicative filtering, modeling factuality as product of claim-level scores, and uses ensemble methods with group-conditional calibration for more accurate factuality scoring.
contribution: MACI consistently achieves user-specified coverage with substantially higher retention and lower time cost than baselines, providing distribution-free factuality guarantees.

problem: Euclidean space embeddings of hierarchical code structures cause significant distortion, especially for deep or highly branched ASTs, limiting models' ability to capture deep program semantics.
approach: Proposes HypeCodeNet, a geometric deep learning framework operating natively in hyperbolic space with manifold-aware components including hyperbolic embedding, tangent-space message-passing, and geodesic-based attention.
contribution: Significantly outperforms Euclidean models (GraphCodeBERT) on code clone detection, completion, and link prediction, especially on tasks requiring deep structural understanding.

problem: Multimodal LLMs struggle with aesthetic assessment due to scarcity of aesthetic reasoning data and inherent subjectivity, making it difficult to generate accurate judgments with interpretable rationales.
approach: Proposes Aes-R1, integrating AesCoT pipeline for high-quality chain-of-thought aesthetic reasoning data with Relative-Absolute Policy Optimization (RAPO) jointly optimizing absolute score regression and relative ranking.
contribution: Improves backbone PLCC/SRCC metrics by 47.9%/34.8%, surpassing similar-scale baselines and enabling grounded aesthetic scoring and reasoning in unified framework.

problem: Signal integrity analysis in IC design requires expensive SPICE simulation to evaluate crosstalk-induced delay and transient glitches, becoming prohibitive for large-scale designs.
approach: Proposes Si-GT, a graph transformer with virtual NET tokens, mesh pattern encoding, and intra-inter net attention to efficiently model signal propagation and coupling in interconnects.
contribution: Outperforms GNN and transformer baselines on 200k delay and 187k glitch examples with substantially reduced computation compared to SPICE, enabling scalable IC verification.

problem: The expressive power of linear attention layers for in-context learning of linear dynamical systems in non-i.i.d. settings remains poorly understood.
approach: Provides optimal weight construction for single linear-attention layer and proves equivalence to one gradient descent step with autoregression objective; uncovers relation to Preconditioned Conjugate Gradient for larger window sizes.
contribution: Adds to understanding of transformer expressivity as in-context learners and offers plausible hypotheses for observations where they compete with Kalman filters in LDS settings.

problem: Existing neural rendering methods achieve high fidelity but suffer from low rendering speeds or only support pinhole camera models, lacking support for complex lenses and LiDAR data needed for autonomous driving simulation.
approach: Proposes SimULi, extending 3DGS with LiDAR support via automated tiling for arbitrary spinning LiDARs, ray-based culling, and factorized Gaussian representation for cross-sensor consistency.
contribution: Renders 10-20x faster than ray tracing and 1.5-14x faster than prior rasterization while matching or exceeding fidelity, handling wide camera model range on autonomous driving datasets.

problem: AI-based film generation systems generate videos but struggle with expressive camera language and cinematic rhythm, producing templated visuals and unengaging narratives.
approach: Introduces FilMaster, integrating real-world cinematic principles through scene-level retrieval-augmented generation for coherent camera planning and audience-aware post-production rhythm control.
contribution: Generates professional-grade, editable films by learning cinematography from 440,000 real film clips and emulating professional post-production workflows for coherent visual storytelling.

problem: Graph neural networks struggle with heterophilic graphs where connected nodes have dissimilar features, with existing approaches focusing on architecture without addressing root causes and performing worse than MLPs.
approach: Proposes GRAPHITE, directly transforming the graph by creating feature nodes to facilitate homophilic message passing between nodes sharing similar features, based on exact homophily definition.
contribution: First method explicitly transforming graphs to improve homophily, significantly outperforming 23 latest GNNs on heterophilic datasets where even MLPs surpass traditional graph methods.

problem: Adapting multiple pretrained medical foundation models to joint diagnosis across heterogeneous domains (radiology and pathology) remains an open challenge for multi-modal clinical workflows.
approach: Proposes CTF, using clinically grounded concepts as shared semantic interface for cross-modal co-adaptation before fusion, with Global-Context-Shared Prompt mechanism capturing domain-specific priors and cross-domain context.
contribution: Outperforms unimodal and fusion baselines (AUC 0.903 on TCGA-GBMLGG) while requiring only 0.15% additional parameters, enabling parameter-efficient multi-modal medical analysis.

problem: Diffusion models lack ability to interpret and follow numeric instructions for continuous semantic attribute control, as text encoders are designed for discrete tokens and existing methods overlook compositional nature of aesthetics.
approach: Introduces AttriCtrl, decomposing aesthetic attributes and quantifying via hybrid strategy mapping dimensions to [0,1] scale, then transforming user values to embeddings via plug-and-play value encoder.
contribution: Achieves accurate and continuous control over single and multiple aesthetic attributes in diffusion-based generation with generalizable framework.

problem: SE(p)-invariant alignment methods face high computational costs or lack metric guarantees when comparing distributions on measured Banach spaces.
approach: Introduces SEINT, using polar transport discrepancy with distance convolution to extract SE(p)-invariant representations for optimal-transport-based distribution alignment with O(n log n) to O(n²) complexity.
contribution: Proves SEINT is well-defined metric with SE(p)-invariance, outperforms existing methods in classification and cross-space tasks, and enhances molecular generation as regularizer.

problem: Mean flow enables 1-NFE generation but results are often not compelling enough for practical applications requiring higher quality outputs.
approach: Proposes RMFlow, integrating coarse 1-NFE MeanFlow transport with tailored noise-injection refinement, training via new loss balancing Wasserstein distance and sample likelihood.
contribution: Achieves near state-of-the-art results on text-to-image, context-to-molecule, and time-series generation using only 1-NFE at computational cost comparable to baseline MeanFlow.

problem: Video reasoning with reinforcement learning relies on coarse sequence-level rewards and single-factor token selection, neglecting fine-grained links among visual inputs, temporal dynamics, and outputs.
approach: Proposes Video-KTR, performing selective token-level RL using three attribution signals: visual-aware tokens via counterfactual masking, temporal-aware via frame shuffling, and high-entropy tokens for uncertainty.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on Video-Holmes (42.7%, surpassing GPT-4o) with consistent gains on reasoning and general tasks, improving accuracy and interpretability via modality-sensitive token-level updates.

problem: LLMs perform well on single-language code generation but their ability to generate cross-programming-language interoperating code remains underexplored and poorly benchmarked.
approach: Introduces CrossPL, a benchmark covering 2534 cross-programming-language tasks across IPC (six languages) and Python-C FFI modes, with LLM-based workflows for benchmark construction and evaluation.
contribution: Evaluates 20 state-of-the-art LLMs, revealing clear limitations with best model achieving only 19.5% Pass@1 on FFI subset, underscoring urgent need to improve cross-language code generation.

problem: Guidance of generative flow models typically requires modifying probability flow vector field, which restricts flexibility and may introduce errors through field approximation.
approach: Proposes SGFM, modifying source distribution directly while keeping pre-trained vector field intact, reducing guidance to sampling from source distribution with flexibility in sampling method choice.
contribution: Theoretically recovers desired target distribution exactly with Wasserstein error bounds for approximate sampling/field, demonstrates effectiveness on 2D benchmarks, physics tasks, and imaging inverse problems.

problem: Large foundation models have substantial memory requirements, but linear low-rank approximation suffers significant information loss from rank truncation and struggles with adaptive compression across heterogeneous layers.
approach: Proposes NLA, using piecewise-linear kernels with forward-pass optimization to approximate weights and cubic sparsity scheduling to adaptively allocate compression across layers with different sensitivities.
contribution: Demonstrates superior compression performance on LLMs and vision models across datasets while achieving higher compression ratios than existing methods.

problem: Neural network layer widths are typically selected manually or via expensive hyperparameter search, which is infeasible for foundation models with billions of parameters.
approach: Introduces technique to learn unbounded width during training via standard backpropagation, jointly optimizing layer width and parameters across diverse data domains.
contribution: Shows width adapts to task difficulty with easy truncation at zero cost, enabling smooth performance-compute trade-off or dynamic compression without performance degradation.

problem: Existing learning-based data augmentation methods rely on learning latent representations with generative models, lacking intuitive construction and fine-grained controllability.
approach: Proposes data augmentation based on energy-based modeling and information geometry principles, enabling geometrically aware latent space construction with efficient encoding/decoding.
contribution: Achieves competitive downstream performance while offering fine-grained controllability lacking in existing augmentation literature.

problem: Vision-language models are evaluated on comparative reasoning with large, salient differences, but ability to distinguish subtle variations across diverse domains (industrial, medical, aerial) remains unexplored.
approach: Introduces VLM-SubtleBench, evaluating subtle comparative reasoning across ten difference types and diverse domains, with controlled analyses revealing performance degradation patterns.
contribution: Reveals systematic gaps between VLM and human performance on subtle differences, establishing foundation for advancing toward human-level comparative reasoning.

problem: Reinforcement fine-tuning suffers from reward over-optimization where models hack reward signals to achieve high scores without producing quality outputs, particularly in high-reward region.
approach: Proposes rubric-based rewards that leverage off-policy exemplars while remaining insensitive to their artifacts, with workflow to distinguish great and diverse responses capturing high-reward tail.
contribution: Demonstrates rubric-based rewards substantially mitigate reward over-optimization and deliver effective LLM post-training improvements.

problem: Extending unified multimodal understanding and generation to 3D scenes from multiview images, with unclear principles for how generation facilitates understanding.
approach: Presents Omni-View, jointly modeling scene understanding, novel view synthesis, and geometry estimation via understanding model, texture module for appearance, and geometry module for explicit constraints.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art score of 55.4 on VSI-Bench while simultaneously delivering strong performance in novel view synthesis and 3D scene generation.

problem: Existing inference-time scaling for LLMs relies on inefficient discrete search or trial-and-error prompting, missing opportunity for continuous gradient-based optimization.
approach: Proposes ∇-Reasoner, integrating differentiable optimization over token logits during decoding via Differentiable Textual Optimization (DTO), leveraging gradients from LLM likelihood and reward model.
contribution: Achieves over 20% accuracy improvement on mathematical reasoning benchmarks while reducing model calls by 10-40%, shifting from zeroth-order to first-order optimization at test time.

problem: Training diffusion models typically requires clean ground-truth images unavailable in many applications, limiting practical applicability to real-world noisy settings.
approach: Introduces MSM, learning partial measurement scores directly from noisy and subsampled measurements, aggregating scores to synthesize fully sampled measurements without clean images.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on unconditional generation and inverse problems using only degraded measurements, with stochastic sampling variant efficiently approximating exact formulation.

problem: Vision-and-language navigation agents suffer from catastrophic forgetting across environments, limiting practical use in continual learning scenarios where agents must adapt to new domains.
approach: Proposes M³E, mixture of macro and micro experts with dual-router architecture separating scene-level reasoning from local perceptual alignment, using dynamic momentum updates to preserve knowledge.
contribution: Consistently outperforms fine-tuning and continual learning baselines on R2R and REVERIE domain-incremental settings, offering parameter-efficient solution for adapting to new environments.

problem: Existing world models require extensive domain-specific training and produce low-fidelity predictions, while video diffusion models on internet data lack action controllability for sequential decision-making.
approach: Presents Vid2World, leveraging pre-trained video diffusion models through video diffusion causalization (reshaping for autoregressive generation) and causal action guidance for interactive world modeling.
contribution: Demonstrates scalable pathway for repurposing video diffusion models into interactive world models across robot manipulation, 3D games, and open-world navigation.

problem: Autoregressive unified models suffer from slow inference due to sequential decoding, while non-autoregressive models suffer from weak generalization due to limited pretrained backbones.
approach: Introduces Muddit, unified discrete diffusion transformer enabling fast parallel generation across text and image via token-level discrete denoising, strong visual priors, and lightweight text decoder.
contribution: Achieves competitive or superior performance to significantly larger AR models in both quality and speed, highlighting pure discrete diffusion's potential as scalable multimodal backbone.

problem: Confidence scores from segmentation models are heuristic and lack rigorous uncertainty estimates, and applying conformal prediction directly ignores crucial spatial correlations between pixels.
approach: Proposes CONSIGN, incorporating spatial correlations into conformal prediction via decomposition to generate meaningful prediction sets with user-specified error guarantees.
contribution: Generates prediction sets with high-probability error guarantees across medical and COCO datasets, significantly improving performance and uncertainty quality versus CP baselines.
theme: Probabilistic methods (Bayesian methods, variational inference, sampling, UQ, etc.)
